dashboard.visible_facts: Teal Local, warm-orange Forwarded and purple Blocked legend keys identify measured series; the selected navigation item also has orange emphasis. Cream/charcoal surfaces and neutral text remain consistent.
dashboard.interpretation: Opus applies the pinned contract literally: non-user-selected metric hues are off-palette and Forwarded reuses orange beyond primary/selection/focus (7). Sol treats chart series as semantic data and judges the base palette/accent use refined (9). The pictures establish data-color use; the two-point brand deductions reflect how narrowly to interpret the data exception, not contradictory evidence about which colors are visible.
dashboard.disposition: Retain both brand vectors. Dashboard data recoloring was already declined and is not reopened. Neither brand score enters quality or progression.

discovered.visible_facts: The page truthfully says DHCP lease discovery is off, names dhcp_lease_file and supplies an underlined orange Settings link as its only content recovery action.
discovered.interpretation: Opus treats an inline link as outside the contract's primary/selection/focus orange roles (7). Sol treats this sole next-step link as the empty state's primary remedy (9). The pinned contract requires guidance and a next action; it does not require empty-state filler or a new button. The disagreement concerns the role assigned to the same visible link.
discovered.disposition: Retain both accent ratings. No filler, navigation redesign, extra action or palette change; these were already declined.

dark_actions.visible_facts: Remove uses warm coral text, while the selected navigation accent is warm orange. On desktop the Add submit is filled orange and separated into its own form; on phone the filled submit is outside the captured area. Labels, placement and component treatment also convey role.
dark_actions.interpretation: Opus's color 7 weights the nearby hues as a semantic-emphasis slip; Sol's color 9 weights text labels and distinct placement/treatment. Pinned dark tokens are --ky-danger #ff8176 and --ky-accent #f5865f. Hue proximity is visible; it does not prove users confuse actions or establish a computed contrast failure.
dark_actions.disposition: Retain both quality color ratings. No functional ambiguity is proven, no shared palette override is required, and palette changes already declined are not reopened.

concrete_finding_audit.finding: R5 cache graph has gridlines without a visible missing-sample explanation.
concrete_finding_audit.verdict: Supported with a precise null-only qualification.
concrete_finding_audit.directly_observed: All four Dashboard originals have an empty cache plot; the 0% headline is a summary, not evidence of 0-valued history samples.

frozen_source.facts: Cache history maps hits+misses==0 to null; a nonzero lookup count maps to the rounded hit percentage, including valid 0. line() skips only null. Hover already says 'no lookups' for null, otherwise '<rate>% hit rate'.

sample_evidence.source: Parent's independent actual R5 local-only fixture/history verification, supplied in task; manifest-04-after.json query_totals corroborate 24 total, 18 authoritative, 6 blocked, 0 forwarded and 0 cached.
sample_evidence.attribution: All actual R5 cache values are null because this fixture bypasses cache. Parent verification is recorded as supplied, not newly executed or reconstructed from the summary.

concrete_finding_audit.correction: Do not call this a failure to draw a valid 0% series, claim hover lacks an explanation, or hide the 0% headline. A future visible explanation may supplement the existing tooltip for a window with no lookup samples.
concrete_finding_audit.boundary: No-data wording applies only when every derived rate is null; any valid zero or positive sample prevents a whole-window no-data label.

concrete_finding_audit.finding: Response time shows a single dot.
concrete_finding_audit.verdict: Visible on the two desktop originals; already handled as a valid sample, not an empty chart or missing lone-sample marker.
concrete_finding_audit.directly_observed: The desktop plots show one teal marker on/near the 0ms line. The phone initial view cuts the lower plot, so its marker cannot be assessed there.

frozen_source.facts: A positive latency_count yields Math.round(sum/count), even when zero; no count yields null. line() already adds r=3 circles to isolated non-null samples; zero remains a sample. Hover says 'no queries' only for null.

concrete_finding_audit.qualification: A future all-null latency window can receive visible and accessible missing-sample wording. The captured desktop window has a sample and must not acquire a false no-data label. Keep the marker and zero values.

concrete_finding_audit.finding: Filtering toggle, Refresh all lists and row actions share quiet outline treatment; Lists gap/hierarchy are weak.
concrete_finding_audit.verdict: Grouping refinement is supportable; the severity of competing hierarchy and gap size is reviewer judgment, not a proven behavior failure.
concrete_finding_audit.evidence: No additional Blacklists image was opened. Existing frozen Opus/Sol rows and reports describe the same old page differently. Frozen template lines 30-38 place separate toggle and global-refresh forms together; lines 50-52 start Lists; lines 67-83 retain independent row toggle/refresh/removal forms.
concrete_finding_audit.qualification: Turning filtering off reduces protection; that does not make it the primary task that must be promoted with orange or a danger treatment. Four equally styled controls do not prove users cannot distinguish their explicit labels. Approximate screenshot gap and form/table width judgments are not exact CSS measurements.
concrete_finding_audit.bounded_candidate: Move the existing global-refresh POST beside Lists as a quiet button, retaining the Filtering on/off action, CSRF field, read-only conditions, row actions and on/off/loading/error states. Treat this solely as the parent's supplied scope; the future implementation was neither read nor evaluated.
